issues.legal_issue: A power of attorney executed abroad for the purposes of registration is valid only if it complies with the authentication requirements in Section 33(1)(c) of the Registration Act.

A statutory presumption of due registration under Section 60 of the Registration Act does not arise where the requirements for execution and authentication of the power of attorney have not been satisfied.
A party seeking a declaration of title must prove the title on which the claim is based, including the valid execution of the conveyance through an attorney.

Whether non-production of the power of attorney underlying a registered sale deed is fatal to proof of the deed and the claimed title depends on compliance with the applicable registration requirements and the other evidence of execution.
A registered sale deed may support a rebuttable presumption of valid execution and the authority of its executant, which may be displaced by evidence to the contrary.

In a second appeal under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the High Court cannot set aside concurrent factual findings by drawing a statutory presumption that is unavailable on the established facts.
